title: Backwards Tour
statement: A walking tour is stored as a linked list of stops from start to finish. Tomorrow's tour runs the same stops in reverse. Return the head of the list in reverse order; the nodes may be reused.
examples: a single stop stays as it is

approaches.name: Turn the pointers around in one pass
approaches.hint: Walk once and change each arrow
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: prev, curr, and a saved next pointer turn every arrow around in one walk, with no copies.

approaches.name: Copy values to an array, write them back reversed
approaches.hint: Use an array as a scratch pad
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and linear, but it needs an array as long as the list.

approaches.name: Recursion on the rest of the list
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Reverse the rest, then attach the first node at the end. Correct, but the call stack grows with the list and can overflow for long lists.

approaches.name: Sort the stops in decreasing order
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Reversing is about position, not value. Sorting only works when the stops happen to be in increasing order.

title: Two Sorted Queues
statement: Two ticket queues are linked lists of ticket numbers, each in increasing order. Join them into one list in increasing order, reusing the nodes.
constraints: Up to 100,000 nodes in each list

approaches.name: Relink with a dummy head and a tail pointer
approaches.hint: Take the smaller front node each time
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each node is attached once by changing one pointer; the leftover list is attached in one step.

approaches.name: Collect all values, sort, build a new list
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but it ignores that both lists are already sorted and makes new nodes.

approaches.name: Attach the second list after the first
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: The result is only sorted if every ticket in the first list is smaller than every ticket in the second.

title: Skip Closed Stations
statement: A subway line is a linked list of station codes. Some stations are closed today, listed by code. Remove every closed station from the list and return the head; the closed codes may include the first station.
examples: 4 → 4 with closed 4 gives an empty list

approaches.name: Dummy node, then unlink in one pass
approaches.hint: Give the head a node before it
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: With a dummy in front, every node, the head too, is removed by changing its predecessor's pointer, in one walk.

approaches.name: Build a new list of the open stations
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and linear, but it makes a second list instead of reusing the nodes.

approaches.name: Find one closed station, remove it, start again from the head
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but each removal walks from the head again, so many closed stations make it slow.

approaches.name: Set the closed stations' values to 0
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: The nodes stay in the list, so the closed stations are still there, just with a wrong code.
